messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: P2 - elevated 5xx and connection errors for inference-rt in us-west-2a (detected at 22:04 UTC). 40% tail latency spike, 15% error rate over last 2m. Auto-escalating to oncall.

maria (oncall-sre): on it. taking ownership. first check: NLB target health + ENI attach errors? can someone paste recent health counts?

jamal: looking. watching NLB target unhealthy count jump around 22:02.

jamal: metrics snippet:
```
region: us-west-2a
nlb_unhealthy: 72 -> 410
socket_errors: 0.5% -> 7.2%
api_5xx_rate: 0.3% -> 14.8%
node_cpu: normal
eni_attach_failures: yes (RateLimitExceeded on ENI attach) from ASG
```

chris: I see a backlog on instance launches in the Dedicated ASG due to ENI attach throttling on that AZ. AWS console shows "ENI attach rate limit exceeded" for the last 6 minutes.

maria (oncall-sre): ok that matches the symptoms — targets go unhealthy, traffic piles up, kvcache miss pressure, model loads time out. immediate mitigation: enable cross-AZ fallback and shift traffic off us-west-2a. @leen can you push a route weight change to shift 70% -> 2b and 30% -> other regions?

leen: on it. updating service routing policy now, increasing weight to us-west-2b and fallback to us-east-1 for burst capacity. will push gradual 20% steps.

deploybot: routing-update job queued: update-service-route inference-rt --weight us-west-2a=0.3 us-west-2b=0.5 us-east-1=0.2

maria (oncall-sre): also toggle sticky sessions off on the ALB/NLB for this service to avoid harmful session affinity while targets are flapping. jamal can you take that?

jamal: disabling stickiness on NLB listener.

jamal: command run:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes \
  --target-group-arn arn:... \
  --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false
```

sophie (support): heads up -> support: customers on low-tier experienced 20-30s timeouts; SLOs for enterprise impacted for a few minutes. drafting comms. anyone have a short status blurb?

maria (oncall-sre): short blurb: "We saw elevated connection errors in us-west-2a causing higher latency and retries for inference. Traffic is being shifted to healthy zones; mitigation in progress. We'll update when all targets return to healthy." use that and tag impacted tenants.

sophie (support): copying into support ticket for affected accounts. thanks.

chris: note: kvcache warmup will take a minute after traffic moves. suggest we route only 50% initially to other zones to avoid immediate cache stampede. we'll use progressive shift: 30 -> 60 -> 90 over 6m.

leen: started progressive policy: set to 0.5 at 22:07, next step at 22:09.

maria (oncall-sre): good. also start model-fallback policy for customers sensitive to latency: switch heavy models to quantized smaller variant in the fallback pool to reduce token latency while we stabilize.

deploybot: rollout-config applied: inference-rt/fallback-models "quant-small" for 25% requests.

jamal: I'm seeing ENI attach errors dropping after shifting weights; unhealthy target count decreasing. current:
```
nlb_unhealthy: 410 -> 98
socket_errors: 7.2% -> 2.1%
api_5xx_rate: 14.8% -> 4.3%
```

maria (oncall-sre): great. leave routing in progressive mode. keep stickiness off until NLB targets fully healthy for 10m.

chris: double-check health checks: some targets still respond slowly to /healthz because model-load timeouts (OOM on startup). I'll increase health check timeout to 10s temporarily to avoid churning.

jamal: ran:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --attributes Key=health_check_timeout_seconds,Value=10
```

sophie (support): drafting customer message update:
"We experienced elevated connection errors in a single availability zone in us-west-2. Traffic has been moved to healthy zones and we expect full recovery within the next 10-15 minutes. If you're seeing errors, please retry — we've applied temporary fallbacks to reduce latency."

maria (oncall-sre): heads-up for oncall handoff: I'm at +30m. if this is still ongoing at 22:35 UTC I'll escalate to a full incident and bring in network ops. @ryan (oncall-next) please stand by to take the handoff in 35m.

ryan (oncall-next): standing by, will join at handoff time.

jamal: NLB unhealthy down to 22, 5xx at 0.9% now. ENI attach errors almost gone. ASG is able to launch new instances for warm pool.

maria (oncall-sre): good sign. begin reversing stickiness change only after 15m of stable healthy counts.

chris: AWS posted a note showing a transient ENI attach throttling event in that AZ; they claim they cleared capacity backlog. keeping an eye.

maria (oncall-sre): preparing post-incident notes: cause = AZ ENI attach rate limiting/backlog leading to target failure and NLB churn -> degraded inference. Mitigations = traffic shift, disable stickiness, increase health timeouts, fallback models, progressive routing. Impact = 10-15 min of elevated latency and error for a subset of requests, support notified.

sophie (support): posted update to affected customers and updated internal status doc.

jamal: final checks: all targets healthy, no ENI errors for 8m, 5xx back to baseline. rolling traffic back to normal weights slowly.

deploybot: routing-update job queued: restore-service-route inference-rt --weight us-west-2a=0.6 us-west-2b=0.3 us-east-1=0.1

maria (oncall-sre): OK rolling back. keep monitoring for 30m. I'll do handoff to @ryan with summary and runbook notes in 10m.

ryan (oncall-next): thanks — I will monitor the next hour and will open an incident if error rate rises again.

maria (oncall-sre): handing off now. summary:
- root cause: transient AZ ENI attach throttling -> NLB target flaps
- immediate mitigations: traffic shift, disable stickiness, increase health timeouts, model fallbacks
- action items: follow up with AWS support for ENI quota/behavior, consider pre-warming ENI attachments in ASG, update runbook to include progressive kvcache warm steps

ryan (oncall-next): received. taking over.

incident-bot: Incident: resolved (status: recovered). Duration: ~34 minutes. Incident owner: maria. Follow-up: aws-ticket-98321 opened for ENI capacity follow-up.

maria (oncall-sre): closing thread. will add postmortem with timeline and metrics in #postmortems later. thanks all for the quick triage and support :thumbsup:
